title: Range-split bit-packed exhaustive GPU scorer (Version A)
question: What is the batch-1 latency and index size of an exhaustive exact scorer over a range-split, bit-packed inverted index?
hypothesis: The scorer returns the canonical top-k for every calibration query; its latency relative to the published baselines is empirical.
motivation: The 2026-11-12 study found the adapted GPUSparse monolithic path 2.9-3.5x faster than the CSR full-byte pruner. This tests a different scoring/payload layout: an inverted index cut into document ranges that are scored in shared memory.

declared_changes.new_index_layout: term-major blocks per (term, document range); bit-packed in-range gaps; uint8 impacts
declared_changes.new_scorer: one thread block per range with uint32 shared-memory scores, local top-k, single-block merge
declared_changes.shared_code_modified: none; cuda_topk.cuh and cpu_pilot.cpp are included unchanged

timing_boundary: sparse query construction, query upload, both kernels, top-k download, event synchronisation; index build/load/upload, validation gate, file writes and CPU checks excluded
correctness_rule: zero ordered-ID or score mismatch against cpu_pilot score for every checked query
measurement_and_analysis_plan: configs/protocol.json: cuda5 RTX 4070, 1M documents, k=10, batch 1, 3 processes, 3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds, per-query medians, pooled median with crossed bootstrap interval; comparison with published baseline medians is exploratory, different session, not paired
success_rule: Correct on all fixtures and all 500 calibration queries at 100K and 1M; timing completes under the registered protocol.
failure_rule: Any mismatch is a recorded failure and blocks timing. Higher latency than the published baselines is a valid negative result.
next_if_negative: Use a kernel-time breakdown to decide between layout changes, range-level pruning (Version B) or stopping.
recording_ids: not recorded by the team runtime
